action_criteria.expected_evidence: TSH, folate, RPR and HIV normal or negative; B12 268 pg/mL (low-normal) after 16 years of metformin; HbA1c 8.6%; LDL 96 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40 mg; eGFR 53
action_criteria.label: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, HbA1c, lipid panel)
action_criteria.rationale: Reversible contributors are excluded (including the low-normal B12 on metformin), and the glycaemic, lipid and renal values set her vascular management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Fazekas 3 white matter hyperintensity with five lacunes and two deep microbleeds together with Scheltens MTA grade 3 and temporoparietal atrophy; no DESH, callosal angle 112 degrees
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms (FLAIR with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI for chronicity, SWI for microbleeds and siderosis) together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
action_criteria.rationale: Both the small-vessel burden and the atrophy grade have to be measured, and the ventricles assessed for hydrocephalus given the gait and urinary symptoms.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positive: CSF Abeta42/40 ratio 0.036 with phospho-tau181 112 pg/mL, or a positive amyloid PET (Centiloid 96)
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF Alzheimer biomarkers or amyloid PET: a Fazekas 3 burden already explains a vascular dementia, and the biomarker shows whether Alzheimer pathology coexists
action_criteria.rationale: A storage-type amnesia with MTA grade 3 beside a severe small-vessel burden is the mixed question one amyloid biomarker answers.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not stop the work-up once the vascular burden is found to be sufficient: sufficiency for one diagnosis is not exclusivity.
Do not withhold a cholinesterase inhibitor because a vascular diagnosis has been made, when Alzheimer pathology is biomarker-confirmed.
Do not omit vascular risk-factor treatment because the amnesia looks typical of Alzheimer disease.
Do not pursue tight glycaemic targets that risk hypoglycaemia in a densely amnestic patient.
Do not prescribe anticholinergic bladder agents for the urinary urgency.
required_recommendations: Name mixed dementia with both components severe: Alzheimer disease (storage-type amnesia, MTA grade 3, positive amyloid biomarker) and subcortical small-vessel disease (Fazekas 3, five lacunes) [VASCOG_2014].

Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for the Alzheimer component (e.g. donepezil 5 mg at night, 10 mg after 4-6 weeks if tolerated), watching for worsening urinary urgency, bradycardia and falls [NICE_NG97].
Continue clopidogrel 75 mg daily as single antiplatelet therapy after the lacunar strokes; two deep microbleeds do not contraindicate it [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary].
Lower blood pressure gradually to below 130/80 mmHg (156/84 on perindopril and indapamide), checking orthostatic blood pressure at each change because she falls [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary].
Increase atorvastatin to 80 mg daily, high-intensity statin therapy after ischaemic stroke (LDL 96 mg/dL on 40 mg) [AHA_ASA_2021_secondary].

Individualise the glycaemic target to about below 8.0%, relaxed further as the dementia advances, and avoid hypoglycaemia; HbA1c 8.6% on metformin and sitagliptin can be improved with an agent of low hypoglycaemia risk [ADA_older_adults_2026].
Replace vitamin B12 (268 pg/mL after 16 years of metformin, with reduced ankle vibration), or confirm deficiency with methylmalonic acid first.

Address falls (physiotherapy, home hazard review), urinary urgency (exclude infection, timed voiding) and carer support, and discuss the faster progression of mixed dementia and advance care planning with her husband [NICE_NG97].

avoided_actions.rationale: A steady five-year decline without fluctuation or episodes: EEG answers no question in this patient.
Hypomimia alone, without rest tremor, rigidity, fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: a dopamine transporter scan answers no question in this patient.
No core feature of Lewy body disease; cardiac sympathetic imaging answers no question in this patient.
A steady five-year decline is not the subacute multidomain syndrome that indicates paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis antibodies.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
Two lacunar infarcts and no cortical or territorial infarct on MRI: there is no embolic pattern for an echocardiogram to explain.
Lacunar infarcts from small-vessel disease without a cortical or territorial infarct: prolonged rhythm monitoring would not change the diagnosis or the treatment.

accepted: Mixed Alzheimer and vascular dementia, both components severe: biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer pathology with severe hypertensive small-vessel disease

differential.key_features: The Fazekas 3 burden with five lacunes would suffice for this diagnosis in isolation, and the gait disorder and dysexecutive syndrome fit it, but small-vessel disease does not produce a dense storage-type amnesia with impaired recognition, and the amyloid biomarker is strongly positive

The storage amnesia, MTA grade 3 and a strongly positive amyloid biomarker would suffice in isolation, but Alzheimer disease does not produce a Fazekas 3 burden with five lacunes, extensor plantar responses or this gait disorder

Gait, urinary urgency and cognitive impairment are all present and the Evans index is 0.31, but the temporal horn enlargement follows the hippocampal atrophy, there is no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space and the callosal angle is 112 degrees
No fluctuation, hallucinations, spontaneous parkinsonism or dream enactment despite the hypomimia
B12 268 pg/mL is low-normal after 16 years of metformin and worth replacing or confirming with methylmalonic acid, but it explains none of this syndrome

key_clinical_evidence: A vascular burden sufficient to explain a dementia does not exclude a second pathology, and this case is built to punish stopping there: the storage amnesia is the finding that demands the biomarker
The two profiles are independently severe, which is the argument for two pathologies rather than one pathology with a secondary feature
Recognition memory is the discriminating test: small-vessel disease impairs retrieval more than storage
Mixed pathology is the commonest substrate of dementia at this age and it progresses faster than either component alone, which is information the family needs
Both treatment plans are indicated, and the failure mode is applying only the one that matches the label chosen first

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Sufficiency is not exclusivity: the dense storage-type amnesia with impaired recognition is not produced by small-vessel disease, and the biomarkers are strongly positive
red_herrings.data_point: A Fazekas 3 burden with five lacunes, sufficient on its own for a vascular diagnosis
red_herrings.intended_effect: Closes the diagnosis as vascular dementia and makes the biomarker look unnecessary

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The husband reports that neither stroke coincided with a cognitive step and that the decline has been steady, the temporal signature of a degenerative process running alongside the vascular one
red_herrings.data_point: Two lacunar strokes in the history
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the diagnosis on a stepwise vascular course

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Marta Lupi is a 74-year-old retired secretary whose husband describes five years of decline that he cannot fit into a single pattern. The forgetting came first and has been the most disabling feature throughout: she forgets conversations entirely, cannot retain a message for five minutes, and does not recognise that she has been told something even when reminded of the circumstances. At the same time she has become progressively slower and more disorganised, cannot sequence a task, and has stopped cooking. Two lacunar strokes, six and three years ago, each produced transient symptoms with full clinical recovery, and her husband does not think either coincided with a step in her cognition — the decline has been steady throughout. Walking changed three years ago: small steps, occasional falls, and urinary urgency. Her father had vascular dementia after a stroke and her mother had a dementia from 78. She has hypertension, diabetes and hyperlipidaemia, all imperfectly controlled. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment.
